What the Cobb County clerk records

The Clerk of Superior Court is the county's official keeper of land records. Deeds, plats, condominium floor plans, liens, UCC filings, general execution docket entries, military discharges, trade names and partnerships all get filed here. The Real Estate Division is the desk where your deed to a buyer lands, and where the cancellation of your old security deed shows up after the loan is paid off.

The office is in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta, next to the State Court Building. Recording happens upstairs on the second floor, and copies come from the deed room on the first. Mail goes to P.O. Box 3430, Marietta, GA 30061. Hours run 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays, but the recording and copy counters close half an hour earlier. The phone number is 770-528-2000.

Mail pickup between the Postal Service and the county mail room has shifted. Anyone racing a deadline should mail early and avoid e-filing late in the afternoon on the final day.

Who can file a deed on paper?

Georgia House Bill 1292 took effect January 1, 2025. People filing for themselves must now e-file real estate documents. Every e-filer first passes identity verification, photo check included, on the Clerks' Authority portal at efile.gsccca.org, and that portal is the only place real estate documents can be e-filed.

Paper filing remains open to these groups:

  • Attorneys admitted in Georgia
  • Mortgage lenders, whether they hold a Georgia license or are exempt
  • Mortgage servicers
  • Surveyors holding a Georgia license
  • Title insurance companies holding a Georgia license
  • Real estate brokers and salespersons holding a Georgia license
  • Any public official

Anyone in those groups who chooses to e-file still has to be verified. A seller who works through a closing attorney or title company rarely touches the filing, since the closing office submits the deed. The person most affected is an owner who prepares and files a deed without an attorney. Finish the identity check well before the recording date.

Recording fees

A deed costs $25.00 for the first page and nothing for pages after that. Security deeds, assignments, satisfactions and cancellations fall under the same line. The clerk's site has an online fee calculator that gives the exact total for a filing. The counter accepts cash, money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks and cards. A cardholder paying in person must show ID and sign the charge slip.

Selected real estate filing fees at the Cobb County clerk

Deeds, security deeds, assignments, satisfactions, cancellations$25.00$0.00
Plats$10.00$10.00
Liens, lis pendens, notices of commencement, fi. fas.$25.00$0.00
State and local tax liens and releases$5.00$2.00
Bonds and landlord bonds$25.00$0.00

Extra cancellations, releases, satisfactions and assignments are priced per document. One check can cover the recording fee and the transfer tax, except for trade names. Make it out to the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court.

Georgia transfer tax and how it is paid

Warranty deeds and quit claim deeds both come in with a PT-61 form and the transfer tax, paid at recording unless an exemption applies. The clerk cites O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and 48-6-2. You complete the PT-61 online and print it to hand in with the deed, or use the computers in the lobby.

The rate is $1 on the first $1,000 of the sale price, then 10 cents for every further $100, with any fraction counted as a full unit. By law the seller owes it, though many contracts shift it to the buyer. The settlement statement shows who paid.

Lenders face a separate charge, the intangible recording tax on a long-term note secured by real estate, set at $1.50 per $500 of the note. A security deed must be filed within 90 days of signing to avoid penalty and interest when the note runs past three years or is not exempt. That deadline is the buyer's lender's worry far more than yours.

What a deed must include

Warranty deeds and quit claim deeds need the same items: the full legal description, the name of the party giving the property, the name of the party receiving it, and the grantor's signature with a witness and a notary. Nobody at the clerk's counter notarizes, so bring a deed already completed before a commissioned Georgia notary.

The two types protect a buyer differently. A warranty deed is the usual choice in a purchase. It guarantees that title is good and marketable, which is why buyers and lenders ask for it. A quit claim deed passes only whatever interest the signer holds, with no promise that title is clear or free of liens, and it tends to appear in transfers between relatives or into a family entity.

  • Copy the full legal description from your last deed rather than using the street address.
  • Have the notary and the witness sign in the same sitting as the grantor.
  • Complete the PT-61 before you arrive.
  • Bring one payment that covers the recording fee and the tax.

Getting copies and confirming your old mortgage was cancelled

There are three ways to get a recorded document. Print it from the clerk's website, copy it in the first-floor deed room, or mail in the request form with a self-addressed stamped envelope. Condo floor plans follow the same routes.

After a payoff, the cancellation of a security deed normally goes back to the borrower unless the lender directs it elsewhere, which usually means the mortgage company. Search the clerk's site to confirm the cancellation was filed. Lien payments never go through this office. They go to the lien holder.

Permits for fences, additions and similar work come from another office, either Cobb County or the City of Marietta, whichever covers the address. The clerk's real estate page also links to the Filing Activity Notification System at fans.gsccca.org.

Selling a house in Cobb County

Cobb sits northwest of Atlanta, with Marietta as the county seat. The 2020 population was 766,149. The tax commissioner's office bills the county and school district, and the cities of Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna and Powder Springs bill their own taxes.

For a seller, the clerk's office matters at two moments. One is when the deed to your buyer is recorded. The other is when the old loan's cancellation is filed. Liens that must be released before a deed can be recorded are a job for a closing attorney, because the clerk's staff cannot advise you. A cash sale to a buyer who closes quickly still needs the same recorded deed, transfer tax form and payment, so none of this goes away. It is just handled on a shorter calendar.

Frequently asked questions

Which Cobb County office takes a deed for recording?

The Real Estate Division of the Clerk of Superior Court, in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta. Doors open weekdays at 8:30, the recording counters stop at 4:30 and the office closes at 5:00. Questions go to 770-528-2000.

Can I file my own deed on paper in Cobb County?

Usually not. Since January 1, 2025, people filing for themselves must e-file at efile.gsccca.org after a photo identity check. Attorneys, lenders, servicers, surveyors, title companies, brokers and public officials may still file on paper.

What does recording a deed cost in Cobb County?

The charge is $25.00 for the first page and nothing for added pages. Transfer tax is extra and goes in with the PT-61 form. The online fee calculator gives an exact total, and one check can cover both.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Cobb County sale?

The law puts it on the seller, and the sales contract may move it to the buyer. The rate is $1 on the first $1,000 of the price plus 10 cents for each further $100. The settlement statement shows who paid.

Does the Cobb County clerk notarize or give legal advice?

No on both counts. The clerk's office does not notarize, so bring a deed already signed before a notary with a witness. Clerk staff also cannot advise on what a deed should say, so ask a closing attorney.

What the DeKalb County clerk does at a home sale

Recording the deed that carries title from seller to buyer falls to the clerk's Real Estate Division, along with mortgages, plats, liens and other papers that touch land in DeKalb County. The office receives more than 204,500 real estate documents a year, and its records run back to 1842 because earlier books burned in a fire.

The clerk acts as clerk of court, registrar of land records, and collector of intangible and transfer taxes. One office handles the recording, the transfer tax certification and the public index that a title examiner searches before closing.

The county seat is Decatur, and the county had an estimated 774,394 residents in 2025.

Where the Real Estate Division is and when it opens

The division is on the ground floor at 556 N. McDonough Street, Decatur, GA 30030. Call 404-687-3812 for real estate records. Weekday hours run from half past eight in the morning until five in the afternoon. The clerk's general information line is 404-371-2836.

Property records can be searched online through the county's deed search and in the public access room. Searches go fastest when you have three facts in hand:

  • The buyer's name (grantee) and the seller's name (grantor)
  • The year of the transaction
  • The tax parcel ID, which every conveyance filed here must now carry

Copies by mail need the book type and page number, and the office will not process a request without them. Pay by cashier's check, money order or attorney's check made out to the DeKalb County Clerk of Court. Certified copies can also be ordered through the eCertification portal, where an approved request must be paid within six days or it is rejected automatically.

  • Certified copy: $2.50 for the first page, 50 cents for each added page
  • Regular copy: $1.00 per page
  • Plat copy: $2.00 per page
  • Card payments carry a surcharge of 2% plus $1.00

Deeds must be filed electronically

Since January 1, 2025, Georgia House Bill 1292 has required every real estate document in DeKalb County to be filed electronically. Mail-in and walk-in recording is closed to new filings. The clerk accepts e-recordings from approved providers, including Simplifile and CSC.

Anyone who is a party to the instrument and files on their own must also upload a government-issued ID at efile.gsccca.org, where it is verified before the filing can go through. O.C.G.A. 44-2-39(b)(1) is the rule behind that step. Most sellers never touch it, since the firm running the closing e-records the deed. If you are selling without an attorney, such as in a family transfer, build the ID check into your timeline.

Plats have been e-file only since 2017, and UCC financing statements became e-file only in 2022.

What goes in the package before the clerk records a deed

Every deed of conveyance needs a PT-61 transfer tax form and the tax parcel ID printed at the top of its first page. Georgia has required that parcel ID on DeKalb transfers and conveyances since July 1, 2019, under House Bill 694.

The PT-61 is completed online at the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority site, printed, and submitted with the deed. The clerk does not supply forms, the document must be complete before it arrives, and most documents need a signature, a witness and a notary. A state-issued ID is required for any filing.

Sellers like one feature: original documents are recorded immediately and handed back, as O.C.G.A. 15-6-72 provides. The recording fees appear on the clerk's Real Estate Fees chart. Georgia moved to flat filing fees in 2020 under House Bill 288, so get the current figure from the clerk or the closing firm instead of an older quote.

Georgia transfer tax: how much and who pays

The seller owes it by law, though a sales contract often shifts it to the buyer. The state rate is $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100.

Payment comes first. The clerk then attaches a certification that it has been paid. The governing statutes are O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10. For questions about exemptions, ask the clerk of superior court in the county.

A separate intangible recording tax applies to a long-term note secured by real estate. The rate is $1.50 per $500 of face value, and in DeKalb the clerk is the collector. A payoff and release on your existing loan is a cancellation of the security deed, and more than 26,500 mortgages are cancelled in the county each year.

Recording deadlines for DeKalb documents

Several documents carry a clock that starts when they are signed or when work ends.

DocumentRuleAuthority
Deed of conveyancePT-61 and parcel ID required; transfer tax due at recordingO.C.G.A. 48-6-1, 48-6-2

Foreclosure deedFile within 120 days of signing to avoid a $500 penaltyClerk's real estate rules

Guarding against a fraudulent filing

The clerk takes part in the Filing Activity Notification System, called FANS, run through the Georgia clerks' authority at fans.gsccca.org. Owners register their own parcels, or those of relatives, and receive an email when a deed, lien or similar paper is filed or indexed against one. Owners who signed up under the older DeKalb alert system had to register again for FANS.

A forged deed or a surprise lien turns up in the title search and can stall a closing. An alert is cheap protection for an inherited or vacant house. A veteran can also record a DD-214 discharge with the clerk at no charge, which keeps a certified copy on file locally.

DeKalb housing figures for sellers

The county had 337,059 housing units in 2025 and 58.8% owner-occupancy for 2020 to 2024. Owned homes had a middle value of $357,800, tenants paid $1,692 in median gross rent, and builders took out 1,321 permits during 2025.

A house in unincorporated DeKalb, in Decatur, in Brookhaven or in Stonecrest all records at the same clerk's office, even though each sits under a different city government.

Timeline for a deed at closing

A typical closing runs in a few steps. The closing firm prepares the deed and the PT-61, adds the tax parcel ID to the first page, and collects signatures, a witness and a notary. The seller's transfer tax is figured from the sale price and paid before recording. The firm then e-records the deed through an approved provider, and the clerk indexes it and returns the original.

When a loan is being paid off, the lender's release is recorded to cancel the old security deed. A new security deed for the buyer's loan should reach the clerk within 90 days of signing. If the seller needs a certified copy afterward, order it through the eCertification portal and pay within six days.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Must a seller travel to Decatur to file a deed?

No. Real estate documents in DeKalb County must be filed electronically, and self-filers upload a government ID at efile.gsccca.org first. The closing firm usually e-records for a sale.

Which side owes Georgia's transfer tax?

The seller is liable under Georgia law, though the contract can assign it to the buyer. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per added $100 or fraction of $100, paid before recording.

When must a security deed or foreclosure deed be recorded?

A security deed should be filed within 90 days of signing, and a foreclosure deed within 120 days, which carries a $500 penalty if missed. Check dates with the closing attorney.

Where can I order a certified copy of a recorded deed?

Order through the eCertification portal, or mail a request listing the book type and page number. Certified copies cost $2.50 for page one and 50 cents for each added page, and an approved portal order must be paid within six days.

What is a PT-61 and why does the clerk require it?

It is Georgia's real estate transfer tax declaration, completed online and printed. Every deed of conveyance in DeKalb County must carry one, plus the tax parcel ID on page one, before the clerk can record it.

What the Douglas County clerk handles

The Clerk of Superior Court's Real Estate Division accepts deeds, liens, plats and UCC financing statements for Douglas County property, then indexes, scans and transmits them. The same division collects and forwards the charges that go with them, including transfer tax and intangible tax. One deed book holds about 1,050 pages.

Other filings in the same office can affect a sale. Federal, state and county tax liens and fi. fa. writs come in through whichever agency issued them. Scanned real estate, UCC and civil protective order papers go on to the statewide cooperative authority, which also posts UCC filings on its website. A veteran's DD214 is recorded at no charge and kept out of public view.

Call the clerk at 770-920-7441 about land records and case files, and Probate Court at 770-920-7249 about wills and estates. Requests for other county documents go through an online JustFOIA portal.

Who can file a deed

House Bill 1292 changed the rules on January 1, 2025. Anyone outside a short list of professions now has to e-file every deed and lien document, and the only channel is the state cooperative authority. An individual homeowner can no longer hand a deed across the counter.

These groups keep their usual access and are not treated as self-filers:

  • Credit unions, mortgage lenders and mortgage servicers.
  • Georgia attorneys and Georgia surveyors.
  • Title insurers.
  • Georgia real estate brokers or salespersons.
  • Public officials.

Self-filers register at efile.gsccca.org, which is their only route. For help, call 1-800-304-5174 or write to help@gsccca.org. In a home sale, the easy path is to let the closing attorney or title company record the deed.

Transfer tax on a Douglas County deed

A deed cannot be recorded until the real estate transfer tax is paid, and the clerk then certifies the payment on the document. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, applied to the sale price.

The seller is liable by law, but contracts frequently hand the cost to the buyer, so read that clause in yours. The PT-61 Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration goes in with the filing and can be completed online through the cooperative authority.

Ask the clerk whether a particular deed is taxable or exempt. Transfer-on-death deeds work a little differently under HB 413. Beneficiaries gain a right to the death certificate, those deeds rank ahead of unsecured debts, revoking one takes one witness rather than two, and no PT-61 is filed at recording. It comes later, when the beneficiary records an acceptance affidavit.

How many documents the clerk records

In 2024 the office recorded 30,047 instruments, 2,296 more than in 2023. Real estate filings and liens make up nearly all of it. A title search on a Douglas County house therefore reads through a thick index, and starting early saves time at closing.

The county has an estimated 154,293 residents and 59,028 housing units. Owners occupy 66.9 percent of homes, and a typical owned home is valued at $296,900.

Recording fees

The clerk's fee sheet covers deeds, liens, UCC filings, plats, copies and civil filings. Its real estate section groups items by kind. Warranty, quitclaim, foreclosure, estate and security deeds sit with modifications, cancellations, affidavits and powers of attorney. Lis pendens, hospital liens, tax liens and lien assignments are a separate group.

Schedules change, so confirm the current amount with the clerk before you budget. Transfer tax is calculated from the sale price and billed apart from recording charges. Everything appears on the settlement statement your closing agent prepares.

  • Recording charge: taken from the clerk's fee sheet.
  • Transfer tax: a state formula applied to the sale price.
  • E-filing for self-filers: arranged through the cooperative authority.

Other Douglas County offices with property records

The clerk holds the recorded title documents, and several other offices hold the rest of a parcel's paper trail. Gathering them before you list answers most buyer questions in advance.

  • Appraisal Department: property record card, assessment notice and appeals, plus the deed specialist who updates ownership on the tax side.
  • Tax Commissioner: the tax bill, homestead exemption file, delinquent tax list and any tax sale notices.
  • Planning and Zoning: survey approvals for splitting or combining parcels and the Unified Development Code.
  • Geographic Information Systems Department: parcel maps and data requests.
  • Records Department: county government records that the clerk does not keep.
  • Probate Court: wills and estate files, relevant when a house passes to heirs.

The Records Department follows the Georgia Open Records Act. It charges nothing for the first quarter hour of staff time, bills later research at the hourly rate of the lowest paid qualified employee, and charges $0.10 per photocopy. Pay by cash, check or money order made out to the Douglas County Board of Commissioners. Staff do not have to create a report or summary that does not already exist.

Dividing a lot or selling the house

Dividing a parcel starts in Planning and Zoning. The proposed survey goes to the Zoning Administrator under Article 5, Section 502 of the Unified Development Code. Once the approved, stamped survey is recorded, the owners sign new deeds and record them through an attorney or the e-file system. The Appraisal Department's deed specialist, at 770-920-7430, handles the tax-record side.

A routine sale moves quickly. The seller signs a deed at closing, transfer tax is paid, and the clerk records the deed with its tax certification. The buyer's lender records a security deed after that. If an old lien or lis pendens sits in the clerk's index, the closing agent will find it and ask for a payoff first.

Heirs, owners with back taxes and landlords with tenants in place sometimes choose a no-repair cash sale. The recording steps are the same, and the buyer's closing attorney does the e-filing, so you never register as a self-filer.

What to gather before closing

A short checklist keeps the recording smooth. Confirm who will e-file the deed, since that should be the closing attorney or title company. Settle the transfer tax clause in the contract so the settlement statement matches. Ask the clerk to check the index for liens against your name or the parcel, and arrange payoffs ahead of time.

If the house came to you through an estate, contact Probate Court at 770-920-7249 for the paperwork that proves who can sign the deed. Bring any survey you have if you are selling only part of the lot.

Frequently asked questions

May I file a deed myself in Douglas County?

Only online. Since January 1, 2025, a person who is not an attorney, lender, servicer, title insurer, surveyor, broker or public official must e-file through the state cooperative authority. The clerk does not take paper filings from them.

What rate does Georgia's transfer tax follow?

It is $1 for the first $1,000, plus 10 cents for each further $100 of the price, counting any fraction as a full unit. The seller is liable, although a contract often moves the cost to the buyer.

Which number covers Douglas County land records?

The Clerk of Superior Court, at 770-920-7441, covers land records and case files. Probate Court, at 770-920-7249, covers wills and estates.

Does a transfer-on-death deed need a PT-61 at recording?

No. Under HB 413 the form comes into play only when the beneficiary later records an acceptance affidavit.

Does the clerk charge to record a DD214?

No. DD214 discharge records are recorded at no charge to the veteran and are kept out of public view.

How the Fayette County clerk fits into a house sale

At closing the clerk files the deed that carries title to the buyer, plus mortgages, releases, liens and plats. The clerk also serves State and Magistrate Courts and, since July 1, 2010, handles the clerical side of the county Board of Equalization, which hears property tax valuation disputes. A seller therefore deals with this office twice over, once for the deed and any recorded lien, and again if a valuation appeal reaches the equalization board.

Fayette counted 125,156 residents in July 2025, about 80.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and a typical owned home is valued at $436,400, so clean title matters to the lenders involved. Deeds for property in Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks, Woolsey and the unincorporated areas all record with this one clerk.

Office address and records hours

The clerk is at One Center Drive, Fayetteville, GA 30214, with a postal box at P.O. Box 130. The main line is 770-716-4290, and 770-716-4291 reaches the Real Estate division.

You can inspect records on weekdays between nine in the morning and five in the afternoon, holidays excluded. Deeds, liens and similar non-court papers are open to inspection under the Georgia Open Records Act, so no formal request is needed during those hours. Public computer terminals inside the office show images without staff supervision.

  • Property index search is on the clerk's Online Services page.
  • A property and mortgage fraud check alerts you when something is recorded against a registered parcel.
  • The court docket search covers Superior, State and Magistrate Courts.

Sign up a parcel for the alert if you hold an empty or estate-owned house, since a forged deed or stray lien is easier to fix when caught early.

Recording fees

The clerk's court fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, charges a flat fee for real estate filings. Call the office to confirm amounts before paying.

Selected Fayette County clerk fees
Filing or serviceFee
Recording a document pertaining to real estate$25.00
Cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment, each instrument listed$25.00
Plat, map or floor plan, each page$10.00
Lien, lis pendens, notice or bond$25.00
Tax lien by a state or local government agency$5.00

Uncertified copies cost $0.50 a page when you copy them yourself and $1.00 a page with staff help. For a certified copy of a deed, the clerk points people to ecert.gsccca.org, and regular copies requested by email run $1.00 per page with payment in advance.

How to check your title record before listing

Pull your own record first. The property index search and the public terminals let you see recorded images yourself.

  • Look for an old security deed that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Look for liens, lis pendens notices and tax liens filed against the owner's name, which carry $25.00 and $5.00 filing fees on the clerk's schedule.
  • Order a certified copy of the vesting deed through ecert.gsccca.org if a buyer's lender asks for one.
  • Check that every name on the deed matches the people signing the listing agreement.

When heirs are the sellers, call 770-716-4291 and ask what must be recorded ahead of the deed to the buyer. Sorting that out first costs less than a delay at the closing table.

Can a Fayette County deed be filed electronically?

Yes, and for many documents it is now the expected route. Since January 1, 2025, with some exceptions, deeds, liens, plats and other real property documents in electronic form are to be filed through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority eFiling Portal. Paper documents go directly to the clerk.

The Online Services page links to eFiling for real estate and UCC documents. Most sellers never touch it, since the attorney or title company running the closing e-records the deed. If you are handling a family transfer without a closing firm, ask the Real Estate division at 770-716-4291 whether paper is accepted for your document before you drive over. Electronic filing is offered in participating counties, so confirm Fayette's current rules with the clerk first.

Georgia transfer tax and the PT-61 form

A deed cannot be recorded until Georgia's transfer tax is paid, and the clerk then stamps a certification onto it. The rate under O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10 is $1 on the first $1,000 or fraction of price, then 10 cents per further $100 or fraction.

The statute puts the liability on the seller, though contracts frequently hand it to the buyer. Exemption questions go to the clerk at 770-716-4290.

The PT-61 declaration is completed online with the Clerks' Authority. Print the finished form and hand it in with the deed; each applicable deed takes just one. Authority customer support answers at (800) 304-5174.

Mortgage payoff and intangible tax

Paying off your lender leads to a release or cancellation of its security deed, recorded here at the $25.00 per instrument shown above. Ask the closing attorney to confirm yours was filed, since a loan still open of record can surface in a title search.

A new mortgage also triggers Georgia's intangible recording tax of $1.50 per $500 of face amount, with the security instrument recorded inside 90 days. Collection falls to the clerk in most counties and to the tax commissioner in others, so ask the Fayette clerk who handles it here. A seller handing over a deed does not owe it.

What happens with a Fayette County sale, step by step

First, the contract is signed and the closing attorney orders a title search that reads the clerk's records. Second, any old security deed, lien or lis pendens must be cleared, and each cancellation is a recording at $25.00. Third, at the table the seller signs the deed and the PT-61 is completed. Fourth, the transfer tax is paid and the clerk stamps and records the deed. Last, the closing firm sends the proceeds and the recorded deed returns to the buyer. A cash sale usually moves faster because no lender package has to be assembled, but the recording steps are the same.

The 770-716-4291 line can tell you what a particular document needs before the closing date arrives. Ask early, because a rejected filing on closing day can push the recording, and the buyer's funding, to the next business day.

Frequently asked questions

What will Fayette County charge to file my deed?

The fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, lists $25.00 for recording a document pertaining to real estate. Releases and satisfactions are $25.00 per instrument listed, and plats are $10.00 a page.

Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Fayette County sale?

The seller owes it unless the contract says otherwise, and the clerk records the deed only after the tax is paid.

Where is the Fayette County Clerk of Superior Court?

The office is at One Center Drive in Fayetteville, with a postal box at P.O. Box 130, Fayetteville, GA 30214. Call 770-716-4290, or 770-716-4291 for the Real Estate division.

Can I look at a recorded Fayette County deed without a formal request?

Yes. Deeds and similar papers are open under Georgia's Open Records Act, so a visit during public hours replaces a formal request.

Does the Fayette County clerk also handle property tax appeals?

Only partly. The clerk keeps the equalization board's files and sends its notices, but valuation appeals begin with the Board of Tax Assessors.

What the Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court records

The Real Estate division answers at 770-781-2120 (choose option 6) or at RealEstate@forsythco.com. The courthouse address is 101 E. Courthouse Square, Cumming, GA 30040. The clerk's website also offers a property index search, a forms page, a link to a property and mortgage fraud check, and a map viewer for abstractors.

Recording fees

Who pays transfer tax on a deed?

Most counties route it through the clerk. Your settlement statement shows whether any of it applies to your closing.

How e-filing a deed works

Real estate e-filers are sent to efile.gsccca.org. Since January 1, 2025, anyone who files real estate documents electronically there must upload government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport, and have it verified before the filing can go forward.

If you plan to bring a deed yourself, call the Real Estate division and ask which filing methods it accepts for your situation, plus how your payment should be made out. The clerk's FAQ page lists questions about checks, card payments, witnesses and notarizing, so read it before you drive to the courthouse.

Liens, tax executions and unpaid property tax

When county tax goes unpaid the Tax Commissioner can issue a Fi.Fa., a lien that lands on the clerk's General Execution Docket. It lasts seven years unless paid off, and the payoff covers the tax plus fees, penalties and interest. A warning letter with a 30-day window comes first.

  • The cancellation is itself a filing at the clerk's counter, with the lien fee shown in the table above.

You can also search the property index on the clerk's website to see whether a cancellation of your old security deed was filed. If it is missing, call your loan servicer first and then the Real Estate division.

Other clerk filings that touch a home sale

The same posted fee sheet lists a few other items owners run into. A veteran who needs a military discharge copy pays nothing but must show valid identification. Notary authentication costs $3.00, and a new or renewed notary commission is $55.00. Registering a trade name for a rental business costs $175.00 as a filing fee, which excludes newspaper publication.

Lawsuits are a separate track. The clerk's civil division in Superior and State Court takes e-filings through two vendors, PeachCourt and a Tyler Technologies portal, and the E-File page links to both. A lawsuit over a sale contract would start there instead of at the Real Estate counter.

Forsyth had 282,805 residents as of July 2025, a 12.5 percent gain since April 2020. Owners live in 84.4 percent of occupied homes, with a median value of $550,400, and the county issued 1,743 building permits in 2025. With values that high, a clean deed and a paid-up tax account matter a great deal to a buyer's lender. The clerk's office is in the courthouse at the county seat, Cumming.

Search the property index for your own name and confirm that every old security deed shows a cancellation. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff if any lien appears. Decide in the contract who pays transfer tax, and fill in the PT-61 online ahead of the signing. Bring photo identification if anyone will e-file for you. A cash closing skips the loan paperwork, yet the deed, the PT-61 and any lien releases are recorded the same way, so the same checklist applies.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Forsyth County deed get recorded?

The clerk's Real Estate division, in Cumming. Phone 770-781-2120 and choose option 6, or write to RealEstate@forsythco.com.

What is the Forsyth County recording charge for a deed?

$25.00 for a deed, quit claim or similar document, and added pages cost nothing extra. Transfer tax is a separate charge.

Who owes the Georgia transfer tax on a sale?

The seller, unless the sales contract moves it to the buyer. The state requires payment before the deed is recorded.

Do I need ID to e-file a real estate document in Georgia?

Yes. Since January 1, 2025, anyone e-filing real estate documents through the Georgia clerks' portal must upload government-issued ID and pass verification first.

Can an unpaid tax bill stop my Forsyth County sale?

It can slow one down. A recorded Fi.Fa. on the clerk's docket is public and stays until the tax, fees, penalties and interest are paid, so get a payoff figure from the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner before closing.

The Deeds and Records Room is on the ground floor of the Lewis Slaton Courthouse in Atlanta and holds instruments reaching back to the early 1800s. The Real Estate Recording customer service line is (404) 613-5313. Mail for the Record Room goes to 136 Pryor St., CG13, Atlanta, GA 30303.

Paper documents are processed within four weeks of receipt. Documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state clerks' authority are processed in two to three business days. Why a Henry County sale ends at the Clerk of Superior Court

Deeds for Henry County land are filed with the clerk's Real Estate Division. Its menu covers Deeds and Liens, Fees, Locating Records, Notary Public, Plats, Trade Names, Uniform Commercial Code filings, Miscellaneous Information and FANS, the Filing Activity Notification System. Until the deed is filed here and the transfer tax is paid, the public record still shows the old owner.

The clerk also runs Civil, Criminal, Finance, Jury and Passport divisions, plus an Administrative Division that holds the Board of Equalization. Appealing your property taxes is one of the tasks listed on the clerk's page, and separate civil and criminal cost schedules are posted.

  • Searching: the Locating Records page covers looking up deeds, liens and property records online.
  • E-filing: the eFile Real Estate Records page routes filers to the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.
  • Costs: the Fees page under the Real Estate Division is where to confirm recording charges before a deed goes in.

Transfer tax on a Henry County deed

Think of the transfer tax as a one-time toll on the sale itself, apart from the yearly property bill. It comes due before recording, after which the clerk attaches proof of payment. Sellers carry it unless the contract assigns it elsewhere.

The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 (or a fraction of $100 to $1,000), then 10 cents for every further $100 or fraction. The PT-61 form words it as tax due at .10 per $100, minimum $1.00. Because the state sets the rate, Henry charges the same as every other county.

Which documents need a PT-61
DocumentPT-61 form needed?
Warranty or other transfer deedYes, even if no money changes hands
Security deed or other debt instrumentNo
Release of a security interest, including a quitclaim used for that purposeNo
Most leases, except an estate for yearsNo
Affidavit such as an in aid of titleNo
Transfer on death deed at recordingNo, but one is needed after the owner dies and the heir accepts

Preparing the PT-61 for closing

Fill it out on the clerks' authority website. The e-filing is free and takes no account. Print the one-page confirmation, carry it to the closing, and if the closing succeeds, hand it in with the deed package. One PT-61 accompanies each deed. Nobody signs it, but the filer ticks a box attesting that the data is true and correct to the best of their knowledge.

  • County is always required, and city matters when the lot lies inside municipal limits.
  • The map and parcel field is mandatory, though N/A is accepted when no number exists.
  • The seller line should name the prior owner rather than a listing agent or auctioneer.
  • A mistake caught after filing goes to the clerk's office. One caught beforehand means a new form and a discarded old one.

The authority's help desk answers at 800-304-5174. Land that straddles a county line needs its own deed and PT-61 in each county, with consideration divided between them and an affidavit describing the split. Exemptions from paying the tax are programmed into the form, which displays the legal basis for any you pick.

Property taxes and recording

The annual property bill is a separate matter, yet a sale touches it. Henry's Tax Commissioner bills the owner of record on January 1 and files a lien against that person unless a settlement statement turns up within 90 days of the due date, under Georgia Code 48-3-3. Statements are emailed to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov.

A third charge attaches to loans. A long-term note secured by real estate must have its security instrument recorded where the land lies, within 90 days, and the intangible recording tax runs $1.50 per $500 or fractional part of the note's face amount. Most counties let the clerk collect it and others use the tax commissioner, so ask Henry's office which one applies before a refinance or a buyer's mortgage closes.

  • Transfer tax: normally the seller's, paid when the deed is recorded.
  • Intangible recording tax: follows the lender's security instrument and does not arise in an all-cash purchase.
  • Property tax: billed to the January 1 owner, backed by a county lien.

Henry County's real estate activity

Henry County has 264,922 residents as of July 2025 and 97,759 housing units on 318.71 square miles of land. With 1,666 building permits issued in 2025, new-build deeds and plats pile up next to resales, which keeps the real estate desk occupied.

Owner-occupied homes are valued at a median of $313,900, and owners live in 74.9% of the 86,704 households. Renters pay a median of $1,674 monthly. The county lies about 25 miles southeast of Atlanta, with McDonough, Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove inside its borders. A deed for a house in any of those cities goes to the same county clerk.

Liens and other clerk services

Liens are the usual surprise. County tax liens and state tax executions are filed in the clerk's office on the general execution docket, and the Henry clerk's court services menu lists Writs of Fieri Facias (FiFa). If a title search turns up a lien, get a payoff figure before closing.

  • FANS: the Filing Activity Notification System has its own page under the Real Estate Division.
  • Notary Public: the Real Estate Division menu includes notary information.
  • Uniform Commercial Code: a separate filing category in the same menu.
  • Trade Names: the menu lists trade name filings for sellers who operate a business under a registered name.

Ask the closing agent whether any judgment, tax execution or recorded lien names the seller. If one does, clear it before the deed is signed and have the release recorded with the clerk afterward.

What to verify before the deed is submitted

Collect the legal description, map and parcel number, and the names exactly as they read on the previous deed. The state form insists on the parcel data. Confirm the transfer tax figure and who is paying it with the closing agent, because the contract can move that cost off the seller.

  • Find out whether the closing agent will e-file or deliver paper.
  • Make sure a payoff and release are lined up for any security deed.
  • Pull the plat if the lot was split recently. The clerk's Plats page covers copies.
  • Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a lien or unpaid current bill exists.

After recording, the deed book and page are cross-referenced to the PT-61 reference number. PT-61 data goes to the state revenue and audit departments weekly, and the form is the trigger for the ownership change on the county tax rolls.

A cash sale has no lender, so no security deed or payoff needs recording, which leaves the deed, the PT-61 and any seller liens as the main items on the clerk's side.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I file a deed in Henry County?

File with the Clerk of Superior Court's Real Estate Division. The clerk's court pages show Deeds and Liens, Fees, Locating Records and an eFile option for real estate records through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

Who pays transfer tax on a Henry County sale?

The seller, unless the contract says someone else will. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per further $100 or fraction, due before the clerk records the deed.

Is a PT-61 required to take a name off a deed?

Yes. Any change in ownership calls for one, even when no money moves, unless the paper is a security deed, a release, a qualifying lease or an affidavit. Some changes also escape the tax itself.

Does a transfer on death deed need a PT-61?

Not when it is recorded, because nothing has been conveyed yet. Once the owner dies and the beneficiary files an affidavit accepting the real estate, the form is needed.

How can I look up a recorded Henry County deed?

Start with Locating Records under the Real Estate Division, which describes searching deeds, liens and property records online. Contact the clerk's office when an older instrument does not turn up.
